topic: Extreme-value calibration for simultaneous causal-isotonic likelihood-ratio bands. Observe iid (W,A,Y) with compact W, continuous A, bounded Y, no unmeasured confounding, strict overlap, and fixed C^s radii with s>3(dim(W)+1) for the W density, treatment density, outcome mean and conditional second moment. On a fixed interior interval assume the causal dose-response is C^2 with derivative bounded above and away from zero and effective score variance nondegenerate. From the cross-fitted AIPW Grenander primitive, define the continuum supremum of local constrained-versus-unconstrained isotonic LR statistics. Prove the canonical Brownian-GCM high-excursion tail, additive ratio, cluster intensity, spatial-volume clock and Poisson/Gumbel limit; then prove primitive-to-LR transfer, feasible volume/variance estimation, calibrated joint profile bands and threshold-crossing confidence sets. Do not claim optimal width, tuning freedom or dominance over the Doss--VandenBerg 2026 multiscale Gaussian bands. Consumer: the AHA/CMS nurse-hours--readmission analysis, where joint profile inference replaces pointwise LR reporting. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Fixed-radius primitive smoothness yields a common Lipschitz modulus for the effective LR variance and boundary-corrected local-polynomial nuisance rates with exponent above 5/12. Foldwise product bias, bounded-variable Gaussian coupling conditions, optimized-LR stability and finite dose-cell reduction were derived. Exact Brownian scaling gives effective spatial length n^(1/3) times the integral of [f theta'^2/(4 kappa)]^(1/3); a finite-energy plateau witness attains LR 1 at energy 9/8, while the true excursion rate remains bracketed and unproved. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the canonical Brownian-GCM LR excursion theorem with sharp declustered high-threshold probabilities, additive tail ratio, constructive centering and a Poisson/Gumbel limit on a growing spatial interval. EARLY KILL TEST: On oracle PAVA windows of radii 4,8,16 and meshes 1/64,1/128,1/256, reproduce the plateau witness and importance-sampled excursion/cluster probabilities at thresholds 4,6,8; a stable failure of localization or additive-ratio scaling triggers an analytic counterexample attempt and stops the spine if verified. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_isotonic_dose_supremum.md

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp high-threshold tail, additive tail ratio, and declustered excursion intensity of the stationary canonical Brownian–GCM local isotonic likelihood-ratio field.

source_refs.claim: Derives the universal Brownian-plus-quadratic-drift GCM likelihood-ratio limit for testing a monotone function at one fixed point.
source_refs.author: Moulinath Banerjee and Jon A. Wellner

source_refs.claim: Obtains sharp extremal behavior for the stationary Brownian-parabolic argmax process, not for the integral-of-squared-GCM-slopes LR field.
source_refs.author: Gerard Hooghiemstra and Hendrik P. Lopuhaä

source_refs.claim: Proves a Gumbel law for the supremum error of Grenander-type slope estimators through an argmax process, leaving LR-functional excursions untreated.
source_refs.author: Cécile Durot, Vladimir N. Kulikov, and Hendrik P. Lopuhaä

open_problems.why_unsolved: The fixed-point LR literature identifies an integral of squared constrained and unconstrained GCM slopes, whereas existing isotonic extreme-value papers control the Chernoff argmax process or slope error. Those statistics do not determine the LR field's rare-event geometry: an exceedance depends on a contact-set rearrangement over an entire Brownian path segment, and nearby exceedances cluster. The first donor-proof step that fails is the Airy-kernel calculation for an argmax crossing; the LR target instead requires a path-space analysis of constrained-versus-unconstrained GCM energy.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For the stationary canonical LR field L(t), prove an explicit asymptotic P{sup_{0≤t≤h} L(t)>u} ~ hλ(u), an additive ratio λ(u+x)/λ(u)→exp(-βx), and a finite positive declustered cluster-intensity constant, uniformly for bounded h and x.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from a shape-constrained testing problem to a canonical Brownian–GCM functional and pivotal inference, while replacing fixed-point calibration with a continuum-excursion problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Pointwise monotone inference has nuisance-dependent cube-root limits -> an LR comparison yields a universal Brownian–GCM law -> simultaneous inference requires the unknown high-excursion law of the entire LR field

method_exemplars.technique: Use Brownian-parabolic transition structure, fixed-window excursion asymptotics, and local-dependence conditions to derive a sharp extreme-value calibration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats the stationary Brownian-parabolic geometry underlying isotonic asymptotics and derives the needed kind of local excursion rate, but for argmax displacement rather than LR energy.

method_exemplars.technique: Establish a Brownian embedding on expanding interior intervals, prove a Gumbel law for the inverse process, and transfer it using uniform localization and jump-spacing bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest existing simultaneous cube-root isotonic limit and supplies expanding-domain and localization controls analogous to those required for the LR field.

open_problems.open_problem: Prove a declustered Poisson point-process limit and constructively centered Gumbel law for maxima of the canonical Brownian–GCM isotonic LR field on growing intervals.

source_refs.claim: Proves an extremal limit for the Brownian-parabolic argmax process using mixing and local excursion conditions, but not an LR-field cluster process.
source_refs.author: Gerard Hooghiemstra and Hendrik P. Lopuhaä

source_refs.claim: Shows that exceedances of dependent stationary sequences can converge through Poisson-distributed cluster locations when suitable mixing and anti-clustering conditions hold.
source_refs.author: Tailen Hsing, Jürg Hüsler, and M. Ross Leadbetter

source_refs.claim: Obtains a scalar Gumbel limit for Grenander sup-norm error, not a marked point process of LR clusters or a constructive LR centering sequence.
source_refs.author: Cécile Durot, Vladimir N. Kulikov, and Hendrik P. Lopuhaä

open_problems.why_unsolved: A marginal LR excursion tail does not determine a simultaneous critical value. One must define clusters through runs or contact sets, prove separation of distant clusters, rule out multiple centers at the rescaled level, and identify the extremal index. Generic stationary-process theorems require these anti-clustering inputs, while the continuous LR field is a non-Gaussian, nonlocal functional of a shared Brownian path. Existing isotonic Gumbel proofs concern argmax or slope-error processes and therefore do not verify the required LR cluster conditions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: With b_T defined constructively by Tλ(b_T)=1 and an explicit scale a_T, prove convergence of the declustered marked LR exceedance process on [0,T] to a Poisson random measure and hence P{a_T(sup_{0≤t≤T}L(t)-b_T)≤x}→exp{-exp(-x)}.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its argument that pointwise cube-root theory is inadequate for whole-curve inference and that an expanding-domain extremal theorem supplies the missing calibration.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Grenander-type pointwise limits behave like near-white noise -> whole-interval inference is governed by rare maxima -> a cluster-aware Poisson theorem yields a usable Gumbel critical value for an LR scan

method_exemplars.technique: Block the index set, identify cluster locations and multiplicities, and prove point-process convergence under separate long-range mixing and local anti-clustering conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested resolution is a limit for positions and marks of dependent high-level LR clusters, the same abstract object treated in this paper.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive fixed-window high-excursion asymptotics from local conditional scaling and combine them with mixing to control maxima over growing intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the closest generic proof template once the LR field's local conditional excursion law has been established.

method_exemplars.technique: Verify local excursion and mixing conditions through Brownian-parabolic process structure and solve the resulting extreme-value centering equation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest isotonic-specific growing-interval extreme theorem and isolates the argument that must be replaced for GCM LR energy.

open_problems.open_problem: Transfer the canonical LR-field Gumbel calibration uniformly to the continuum of constrained-versus-unconstrained LR statistics constructed from a cross-fitted AIPW Grenander primitive.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Pointwise LR convergence localizes at one deterministic dose and only requires ordinary o_P(1) nuisance control. A continuum maximum visits order n^(1/3) effective locations at a growing threshold, so pointwise primitive convergence and a fixed-point argmin mapping are insufficient. The primitive-to-GCM localization must hold over moving random PAVA windows and remain stable after optimizing constrained and unconstrained objectives. A prior CausalSmith review exposed the analogous danger of assuming a load-bearing variation rate without deriving it from an attainable learner class; here that gap must be closed for explicit boundary-corrected cross-fitted learners and then propagated through GCM knot rearrangements. The literature contains smoothing-based Gaussian bands and pointwise shape-constrained LR intervals, but no corresponding extreme-scale causal LR transfer.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For explicit fixed-radius boundary-corrected nuisance learners, prove a uniform high-excursion-scale coupling between the feasible AIPW LR profile and a time-changed canonical Brownian–GCM LR field, including localization, optimized-objective stability, continuum-to-dose-cell reduction, and asymptotic simultaneous profile-band coverage.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its causal estimand, doubly robust LR construction, nuisance discussion, and nurse-staffing application as the starting point while making the fixed-point-to-joint-inference boundary explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Continuous-dose confounding calls for doubly robust adjustment -> monotonicity permits bias-avoiding pointwise LR inference -> scientific scanning of the whole nurse-hours profile requires a uniform LR transfer and simultaneous calibration

method_exemplars.technique: Represent the estimator as the GCM slope of an estimated primitive, establish local asymptotic equivalence after a data-dependent domain transformation, and bound nuisance-induced primitive remainders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The AIPW causal-isotonic object is a generalized Grenander estimator; the new proof must strengthen this pointwise primitive transfer to expanding extreme-value windows.

method_exemplars.technique: Use a uniform Brownian approximation, switching relations, localization, and jump-spacing bounds to transfer an inverse-process extreme theorem to a direct isotonic statistic.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest uniform-transfer architecture, although its direct-statistic argument must be rebuilt for optimized LR energy rather than slope error.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine cross-fitted debiasing with uniform empirical-process approximation and feasible critical-value construction for a continuous causal curve.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its causal nuisance bookkeeping and simultaneous-coverage argument are the nearest estimation-side analogue, with a Gaussian rather than Brownian–GCM limit.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct feasible estimators of the effective LR spatial-volume clock and local score variance whose plug-in error is negligible at the constructive Gumbel-centering scale.

source_refs.claim: Reports a bias-versus-variance problem for estimators of the causal-isotonic scale κ(a) and asks whether a lower-variance doubly robust estimator can be constructed.
source_refs.author: Ted Westling, Peter Gilbert, and Marco Carone
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

source_refs.claim: Its Grenander supremum normalization depends on spatially varying derivative and primitive-variance quantities, showing that inhomogeneous scaling enters global extreme calibration.
source_refs.author: Cécile Durot, Vladimir N. Kulikov, and Hendrik P. Lopuhaä

source_refs.claim: Provides feasible uniform Gaussian bands using estimated nuisance, variance, and bias-correction ingredients, but does not estimate an isotonic extreme-value volume clock.
source_refs.author: Kenta Takatsu and Ted Westling
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: The canonical LR law is pointwise pivotal, but its continuum maximum depends on the effective number of local opportunities, represented by a spatial integral involving treatment density, dose-response derivative, and efficient-score variance. Pointwise consistency of these ingredients does not control the induced error in a logarithmic extreme-value centering. Derivative estimation and cross-fitted conditional-second-moment estimation must achieve a joint uniform rate, and the causal-isotonic literature already documents unstable κ estimation. No located paper propagates a feasible LR-clock error through a constructive Gumbel critical value.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Construct cross-fitted estimators of f_A(a), θ'(a), and κ(a) such that the plug-in clock n^(1/3)∫[f_A(a)θ'(a)^2/{4κ(a)}]^(1/3)da is ratio-consistent at a rate leaving the centered LR maximum unchanged in probability, and prove feasible simultaneous-band and threshold-crossing-set coverage.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its practical account of the scale-estimation bias–variance tradeoff and its requirement that inference remain implementable with learned nuisance functions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal-isotonic limits contain local design and score scales -> pointwise scale estimation already has a bias–variance tension -> simultaneous LR calibration aggregates those scales into a volume clock requiring centering-level precision

method_exemplars.technique: Normalize an inhomogeneous Grenander process by local derivative and time-change factors and convert accumulated local opportunities into the effective length driving a Gumbel law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired clock is the LR analogue of the spatially varying normalization in this Grenander sup-norm theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate conditional variance and smoothness-related quantities under cross-fitting and prove their uniform errors negligible in a feasible simultaneous critical-value construction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats the same causal curve and nuisance functions and demonstrates propagation of feasibility error through a whole-curve band.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a doubly robust pseudo-outcome and regress it on continuous treatment, deriving nuisance-product remainder conditions for the nurse-staffing dose-response application.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the application-matched AIPW signal and nuisance-product structure from which the clock's efficient-score variance must be estimated.

literature_map:
Banerjee and Wellner (2001, Annals of Statistics) establish the universal Brownian–GCM LR law and confidence intervals only at a fixed point.
Groeneboom and Jongbloed (2015, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1407.3491) extend pointwise LR inversion to additional monotone models using Lagrange-modified cusum diagrams.
Groeneboom (1989, PTRF) supplies Airy-function transition kernels for the Brownian-parabolic argmax jump process underlying classical isotonic limits.
Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998, Extremes) prove a growing-interval extreme theorem for that argmax process, including sharp fixed-window tails, but not for the LR energy field.
Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1111.5934) prove a Gumbel law for Grenander sup-norm error under a derivative-away-from-zero regime.
Westling and Carone (2020, Annals of Statistics) give a general primitive-to-Grenander framework with pointwise theory and data-dependent domain transformations.
Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020, JRSSB; arXiv:1810.03269) introduce causal isotonic regression and flag uniform inference and improved κ estimation as open directions.
Kennedy, Ma, McHugh, and Small (2017, JRSSB; arXiv:1507.00747) provide the doubly robust pseudo-outcome route and nurse-hours/readmission application anchor.
Doss, Weng, Wang, Moscovice, and Chantarat (2024, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:2202.03369) give an omnibus doubly robust test for a continuous treatment curve, not joint shape-constrained profile bands.
Doss (2026, JASA; arXiv:2508.08415) develops cross-fitted doubly robust pointwise monotone LR intervals and pointwise flatness adaptation in the same nurse-staffing setting.
Takatsu and Westling (2025, JRSSB; arXiv:2210.06448) construct uniform Gaussian bands for a debiased local-linear causal dose-response curve, providing a neighboring smoothing-based route.
Ai, Huang, and Zhang (2026, arXiv:2602.01595) obtain bootstrap uniform bands for continuous-treatment curves through weighted local-linear estimation.
Sampson, Singh, and Whitaker (2009, JSPI) and Soulakova et al. (2012, Journal of Biopharmaceutical Statistics) give isotonic simultaneous bands for discrete ordered means, not confounding-adjusted continuous-dose LR profiles.
A public Doss JSM 2026 abstract advertises adaptive shape-constrained simultaneous bands but does not state a Brownian–GCM LR excursion, cluster-intensity, or Poisson theorem; no width, tuning, or dominance claim is warranted.
The unoccupied intersection is sharp extreme-value theory for the Brownian–GCM LR functional together with uniform cross-fitted causal-primitive transfer and feasible spatial-clock calibration.
